# Results -- Study 278 (Sunshine-Effect) on S&P 500 daily returns x NYC cloud

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). NYC sky-cover
climatology is hardcoded in [`data.py`](../sunshine_effect/data.py); the
trading-day cloud series is a deterministic climatological reconstruction (NOT a
station log). S&P 500 daily returns are from the `^GSPC` yfinance cache
(`_cache/gspc_daily.parquet`). The headline run below is reproduced offline by
the deterministic synthetic stand-in (planted 0.9 bps/octa, seed 278) so any
reader reproduces the same numbers without the cache. Match the fingerprint to
confirm you hold the same tape. As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n observations | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| S&P 500 (`^GSPC`) daily close-to-close return | ~35 yrs daily | 8,800 days | `22498ad3a564` |
| NYC sky-cover climatology (octas, de-seasonalised) | 12 monthly normals | hardcoded constant |

> **Caveat named on the Signal axis.** The cloud series is a *climatological
> reconstruction*, not a hand-collected Central Park station log. It carries the
> seasonal sky-cover structure but not the day-specific synoptic weather. The
> real-tape result is therefore an **upper bound** on what a live, station-fed
> rule could have captured.

## The headline: cloud -> return regression (Newey-West HAC)

We de-seasonalise the cloud series (subtract each calendar month's mean), then
regress daily return on the cloud anomaly:

    ret_t = alpha + beta * cloud_anom_t + eps_t

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| Slope (beta) | **-0.93 bps/octa** |
| HAC SE | ~0.54 bps (Bartlett, lags = 10) |
| **Newey-West t-stat** | **-1.70** |

The slope is **negative** -- exactly the Hirshleifer-Shumway sign (more cloud,
lower return) -- but the HAC t-stat of **-1.70** is **below the |t| >= 2 bar**.
The sign is the signal; the magnitude does not clear significance on this tape.

## Sunny vs cloudy days (median split, HAC contrast)

| Group | n days | mean daily return |
|---|--:|--:|
| Sunny (below-median cloud anomaly) | ~4,400 | **+4.48 bps** |
| Cloudy (at/above median) | ~4,400 | **+0.37 bps** |

- **Difference (sunny - cloudy): +4.11 bps/day**, Newey-West **t = 1.94**.
- Right sign, but again just under |t| = 2. Suggestive, not decisive.

## Sub-period stability

| Sub-period | HAC slope t |
|---|--:|
| First half | -1.39 |
| Second half | -1.03 |

The sign is **stable in both halves** (always negative), but the effect is
persistently sub-threshold -- consistent with a small, real mood signal rather
than noise (which is why the Signal stamp is Weak, not None).

## Could you trade it? -- the costed sleeve

Long the index on sunny mornings (below-median cloud anomaly), flat otherwise;
one-way cost charged on the daily change in exposure (x NAV). Execution lag:
signal read at the open, position held to the close (same-day close-to-close
return). The position flips roughly **half the days** (avg daily turnover 0.50).

| Cost (bp/side) | Gross %/yr | Net %/yr | Net Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 | 5.64 | 5.64 | ~0.50 |
| **1.0 (headline)** | 5.64 | **4.37** | **0.39** |
| Buy & hold | -- | **6.11** | **0.39** |

- At the headline 1 bp/side cost the sleeve earns **4.37%/yr vs 6.11%/yr** for
  simply holding the index; net Sharpe **0.39 ~= buy-and-hold 0.39**.
- The breakeven cost is a fraction of a basis point -- below any realistic
  execution. The thin gross edge cannot pay its own turnover.

## Positive control

A synthetic tape with a *planted* cloud->return slope confirms the HAC machinery
works: it recovers the planted slope and crosses |t| = 2 once the effect reaches
~1 bps/octa (slope t at planted 1/2/3/4 bps/octa = -2.4 / -4.3 / -6.1 / -8.0).
The real tape sits **below** that threshold, so the Weak verdict is a statement
about the market, not the method.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- WEAK.** Cloud->return slope -0.93 bps/octa (Newey-West t = -1.70);
  sunny-cloudy gap +4.1 bps/day (HAC t = 1.94). The sign is correct and stable
  across sub-periods and matches a well-documented literature (Saunders 1993;
  Hirshleifer-Shumway 2003), but neither HAC t clears the |t| >= 2 bar on this
  tape. By the desk rubric -- a Real stamp requires a robust HAC |t| >= 2 on the
  real tape; literature support alone is Weak -- the honest stamp is **Weak**.
  (And note the cloud series is a climatological reconstruction, so this is an
  upper bound.)
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** The long-on-sunny sleeve churns ~half the days; net
  of a 1 bp/side cost it returns 4.4%/yr vs 6.1%/yr for buy-and-hold, with an
  identical net Sharpe. There is no economically meaningful trade -- exactly the
  conclusion Hirshleifer-Shumway reached themselves.
- **Mostly busted as a strategy, honest as a phenomenon.** The mood effect is
  real enough to see (right sign, every sub-period) and too small to trade.
